brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: A hex-base organizer of 9 pieces (full bases at (0,0), (0,-1), (-2,0), (-2,1); half bases at (1,0), (-1,0), (0,1)) with caps on open faces and joints bolted; check_build reports no issues and meshClash is clear. Whether it is portable (weight, grip, latching) is not something the configurator checks.

requirements.requirement: A base with removable bins for small parts
requirements.evidence: Three removable bins drop into cells: bin hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments) at (0,0), hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments) at (0,-1), and hex-bin-half-e-full-div2 (2 compartments) at (1,0).
drawer:0#0,1#cut (key s, classic style) on the cut face of the half base at (0,1).
handle:-2,0,0;top on a three-cover triangle: covers on (-2,0), (-2,1) and (-1,0). The handle needed all three recesses covered, so the bin-free cells on the west side were used for it.

finish.summary: Built a small hex-base electronics organizer with three removable compartmented bins, one drawer on the south-facing cut half base, and a carry handle on a top-cover triangle at the west end. Caps close the open faces and joints are bolted; check_build is clean with meshClash clear. I did not add props. Material strength, weight and durability are not verified by the configurator.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
